Key Characteristics & Etiology: T-cell mediated podocytopathy peaking between 2-3 years of age; Most common pediatric nephrotic syndrome (>80%)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Loss of glomerular polyanionic charge barrier and foot process effacement causing massive selective albuminuria
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Insidious periorbital/facial edema pitting pedal edema ascites normal/low BP; Red Flags: SBP peritonitis or hypovolemic shock
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Urine dipstick protein >=3+ to 4+ UPCR >200 mg/mmol Serum Albumin <25 g/L; First-line: Oral Prednisolone 2 mg/kg/day for 4-6 weeks

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Immune-complex glomerulonephritis developing 1-3 weeks post-GAS pharyngitis or 3-6 weeks post-impetigo
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Glomerular immune complex deposition causing alternative complement pathway activation and capillary hypercellularity
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Nephritic triad: Macroscopic hematuria (tea-colored urine) facial edema hypertension oliguria; Red Flags: Hypertensive encephalopathy
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Dysmorphic RBCs RBC casts Low C3 complement (<6-8 weeks) Elevated ASO titer; Fluid restriction + Furosemide + Nifedipine

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Uropathogenic Escherichia coli accounts for 80-90% of pediatric UTIs; Female predominant after early infancy
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Ascending bacterial colonization of urinary tract causing bladder/renal parenchymal inflammation
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Unexplained fever irritability poor feeding dysuria frequency loin pain; Red Flags: Septic shock recurrent pyelonephritis
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Urine culture >10^5 CFU/mL clean-catch urine dipstick positive nitrites/leukocyte esterase; RBUS post 1st febrile UTI; Oral/IV Co-amoxiclav or Cefuroxime

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Absolute or relative insulin deficiency in Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus triggered by new onset infection or non-compliance
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Unopposed lipolysis and ketogenesis generating severe anion gap metabolic acidosis and osmotic diuresis
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Polyuria polydipsia weight loss persistent vomiting abdominal pain Kussmaul breathing fruity acetone breath; Red Flags: Cerebral edema lethargy
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Blood glucose >11 mmol/L arterial pH <7.3 HCO3 <15 mmol/L urine/blood ketones positive; IV 0.9% Normal Saline 10-20 mL/kg 1st hour -> IV soluble insulin 0.1 U/kg/h

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Thyroid dysgenesis (agenesis ectopy) or dyshormonogenesis; Most common preventable cause of intellectual disability
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Deficiency of thyroid hormones (T4/T3) required for early post-natal brain maturation and skeletal growth
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Prolonged neonatal jaundice lethargy coarse facial features macroglossia open posterior fontanelle umbilical hernia hypotonia, Red Flags: Severe cretinism
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Elevated newborn screening TSH low free T4; Immediate oral Levothyroxine (10-15 mcg/kg/day) initiated within first 2 weeks of life

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Homozygous beta-globin gene mutations resulting in severe reduction or total absence of beta-globin synthesis
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Imbalanced globin chain synthesis causing precipitation of free alpha chains intra-medullary hemolysis and severe ineffective erythropoiesis
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Severe anemia jaundice hepatosplenomegaly failure to thrive frontal bossing chipmunk facies; Red Flags: Severe heart failure iron overload
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Hb electrophoresis: HbF >90% HbA 0-10% microcytic hypochromic anemia; Hypertransfusion therapy (keep Hb >9.5-10 g/dL) + Iron chelation (Deferasirox)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: X-linked recessive enzymopathy impaired NADPH production leaving RBCs vulnerable to oxidative stress (fava beans drugs infection)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Oxidative denaturing of hemoglobin resulting in Heinz body formation intravascular hemolysis and acute anemia
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Acute intravascular hemolysis 24-48h post trigger dark cola-colored urine jaundice pallor fatigue; Red Flags: Acute renal failure
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: FBC reticulocytosis Heinz bodies on supravital stain decreased G6PD enzyme assay; Avoid oxidative triggers + supportive transfusion if severe

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Most common pediatric cancer (80% of childhood leukemias); Peak incidence between 2 and 5 years of age
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Malignant clonal proliferation of immature lymphoid progenitor cells replacing normal bone marrow hematopoietic elements
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Anemia fatigue pallor petechiae/purpura fever bone pain generalized lymphadenopathy hepatosplenomegaly; Red Flags: CNS stroke testicular mass
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: FBC leukocytosis anemia thrombocytopenia Bone marrow biopsy >=20% (often >80%) lymphoblasts; Combination induction chemotherapy

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Meiotic nondisjunction (95%) translocation (4%) or mosaicism (1%) giving 47 chromosomes with extra chromosome 21
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Gene dosage excess on chromosome 21 disrupting normal tissue organogenesis and neurodevelopment
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Up-slanting palpebral fissures epicanthic folds flat nasal bridge single palmar crease sandal gap hypotonia; Red Flags: AVSD duodenal atresia leukemia
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Karyotype / Chromosomal microarray Echocardiogram (40% AVSD); Early multidisciplinary intervention + thyroid/cardiac screening

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Complete or partial monosomy X (45,X) occurring in 1 in 2,500 live female births
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Lack of second X chromosome causing gonadal dysgenesis (streak ovaries) and lymphatic malformations during embryogenesis
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Short stature primary amenorrhea low posterior hairline webbed neck shield chest widely spaced nipples cubitus valgus; Red Flags: Coarctation of Aorta
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Karyotype 45,X elevated LH/FSH Echocardiogram renal ultrasound; Growth Hormone therapy in childhood + Estrogen replacement for puberty induction
